idiom_name: Rack call(env) app + middleware stack (Rails router as dispatcher)
implementation_notes: The Rack specification defines an application as any object responding to call(env) that returns [status, headers, body], and middleware as an object initialized with the app and delegating @app.call(env) - that is the front controller and its shared chain in two methods. Rails adds the dispatcher: ActionDispatch::Routing::RouteSet matches verb and path to a controller action configured in config/routes.rb. What replaces the classic structure: one Rack object plus a middleware stack replaces the FrontController and Command classes, and controller actions replace command objects, so hand-writing a FrontController class is unnecessary outside server or framework work.
pitfalls: Middleware must not call each on the body: it has to return a new body delegating to the original and close it, or streaming and hijacked responses break at the server boundary.
The response must be exactly a three-element array with a String-keyed header hash; symbol keys or a two-element array fail inside the server, far from the bug.
Rack 3 relaxes several requirements (rack.input need not be rewindable, obsolete keys are gone), so middleware built on Rack 2 assumptions can silently misbehave.
